title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（増崎陽介研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Masuzaki Yosuke)
educationalGoal: This course aims to enable students to define original project themes based on their own interests in architecture, urban space, and real-world society; to analyze and examine these issues through independent and creative approaches; and to synthesize the outcomes into highly original and accomplished architectural works or research papers. Furthermore, the course aims to develop students’ ability to present their work effectively and to communicate their ideas logically and professionally to external audiences.
advice:
The course proceeds through the following stages:

1) Clarification of the research interest
(Information gathering and discussion)

2) Systematic understanding of factors related to the issue
(Information gathering and structuring of the problem)
[Review of previous studies and relevant literature / Field surveys (related cases and case studies)]

3) Establishment of the project theme
[Theme formulation / Site selection / Planning and development of the project execution strategy (including the selection of analytical methods)]

4) Project implementation and final synthesis
[Case studies and analysis / Visualization and structuring of analytical results, proposal development and production of works / Presentation of outcomes (Midterm review in December, Public final review)]
requiredKnowledge:
・The ability to synthesize and integrate the knowledge and insights acquired through previous coursework and everyday experiences
・A critical interest in one’s surrounding environment and the processes by which it has been formed
・A strong drive toward making and creating things

achievementLevels.ideal:
・Students will be able to analyze the design theories and concepts underlying outstanding architectural works, evaluate them from multiple perspectives - including social and historical contexts - and apply and further develop these insights in their own projects.

・Students will be able to structure their personal interests in real society and urban space, establish concrete themes for research, analysis, and design proposals, and present the outcomes as accomplished architectural works or research papers.

              This course aims to enable students to define original project themes based on their own interests in architecture, urban space, and real-world society; to analyze and examine these issues through independent and creative approaches; and to synthesize the outcomes into highly original and accomplished architectural works or research papers. Furthermore, the course aims to develop students’ ability to present their work effectively and to communicate their ideas logically and professionally to external audiences.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              The course proceeds through the following stages:

1) Clarification of the research interest
(Information gathering and discussion)

2) Systematic understanding of factors related to the issue
(Information gathering and structuring of the problem)
[Review of previous studies and relevant literature / Field surveys (related cases and case studies)]

3) Establishment of the project theme
[Theme formulation / Site selection / Planning and development of the project execution strategy (including the selection of analytical methods)]

4) Project implementation and final synthesis
[Case studies and analysis / Visualization and structuring of analytical results, proposal development and production of works / Presentation of outcomes (Midterm review in December, Public final review)]
